records.title: Physics-Constrained Flow Matching: Sampling Generative Models with Hard Constraints
records.review_scope: 36page text read;15selected visual pages;22source claims;not independent review

claims.statement: PCFM applies equality-constraint correction at inference to a pretrained flow model; the objective is the intersection of learned PDE solution support and a specified constraint set.
claims.caveat: A learned support approximation is not an independently measured manufacturing process.

claims.statement: Hard constraint is explicitly qualified as satisfaction up to solver and machine numerical precision, not symbolic zero for every implementation.
A Gauss-Newton step projects onto the linearized affine constraint set; it is an exact feasible projection for affine h with the required invertible Schur system.
claims.caveat: A single step on a nonlinear residual is not generally an exact nonlinear projection.

claims.statement: The reverse approximation uses endpoint displacement and states a Lipschitz/small-step marginal-velocity relation.
claims.caveat: Conditional straight-line interpolants and learned marginal trajectories require separate assumption review; no theorem independently certified here.

claims.statement: Relaxed correction is optional; AppendixH uses lambda0 by default but guided interpolation only for the Heat Table3 setting.
claims.caveat: The lambda0 runtime setting and Heat guided-accuracy setting must not be combined into an unexecuted speed/accuracy configuration.

claims.statement: The final-projection argument assumes twice-differentiable constraints, full row rank near a feasible manifold, a suitable convergence neighborhood, and sufficiently many Newton-Schur iterations.
claims.caveat: No unconditional result for inconsistent constraints, singular Jacobians, every starting point, or fixed one iteration is established.

claims.statement: Benchmarks cover Heat, Navier-Stokes, Reaction-Diffusion and Burgers with numerical/analytical data; models use FNO-based FFM.
claims.caveat: Spatial dimensions and spatiotemporal tensor dimensions are distinct; no factory data or external metrology is supplied by these experiments.

claims.statement: Reported training is 20,000 steps on one V100 for one-dimensional PDEs and 500,000 steps on four A100 GPUs for Navier-Stokes.
claims.caveat: Training hardware is not an inference minimum requirement.

claims.statement: MMSE compares generated/reference ensemble means; SMSE compares ensemble standard deviations.
claims.caveat: SMSE is not standard error, repeated-training variability, or an uncertainty interval on a method difference.

claims.statement: CE averages each sample residual L2 norm over 512 generated samples for one-dimensional problems or100 Navier-Stokes samples.
claims.caveat: Mean CE alone does not establish worst-case compliance or independent physical reference; displayed zeros need raw tolerances.

claims.statement: FPD uses Poseidon-base feature comparisons; Reaction-Diffusion grids are interpolated to128x128 for the pretrained model.
claims.caveat: The table footnote acknowledges interpolation artifacts; feature similarity is not physical residual or calibrated manufacturing accuracy.

claims.statement: The Heat table reports PCFM SMSE0.937 and FPD1.22 versus PDM0.02 and0.17, respectively, despite prose saying PCFM outperforms all methods across these metrics.
claims.caveat: Values are table-display values; MSE columns are divided by10^-2, FPD is unscaled; no significance conclusion.

claims.statement: For Burgers-BC, D-Flow has lower displayed MMSE0.224 than PCFM0.335; ECI has lower SMSE0.089 than PCFM0.123. The Figure5 caption acknowledges slightly worse MMSE/SMSE.
claims.caveat: Exact specified residual and distributional fidelity are different endpoints.

claims.statement: Runtime uses V10032GB, batch32 for one-dimensional problems/batch8 for Navier-Stokes,100 flow steps and lambda0; PCFM per-sample times are291.8,1371.0,636.6 and350.7ms.
claims.caveat: These are not the200-step primary nonlinear fidelity setting or measured industrial throughput.

claims.statement: Final projection shares are1.78% Heat,0.89% Burgers,1.01% Reaction-Diffusion and0.2% Navier-Stokes.
claims.caveat: The prose1-3% range does not precisely cover every table row; extra correction and whole-workflow costs remain configuration-specific.

claims.statement: Printed Burgers mass residuals use constant mass; general solver costs include O(m^2*n) Jacobian/Gram work and O(m^3) Schur solve.
claims.caveat: Current code includes cumulative boundary flux for Burgers; O(n) requires treating constraint count m as small/fixed and cannot be asserted as m scales with n.

claims.statement: The printed Reaction-Diffusion equation uses minus nu*d_x(u), while current generator code uses diffusive flux minus nu*gradient and reaction updates.
claims.caveat: Retain a paper/code formulation discrepancy requiring clarification; do not infer a whole-method failure from a likely printed formula issue.

claims.statement: TVD-inspired equality constrains TV(final) to gamma*TV(initial), with gamma0.3 in the reported ablation.
claims.caveat: This is stronger/specific relative to generic non-increasing TV; it is not a universal physical decay law or manufacturing tolerance.

claims.statement: OOD Burgers changes sigmoid center training0.4-0.6 to disjoint test0.0-0.2/0.8-1.0 and uses200 flow steps; reported PCFM MMSE1.83/SMSE1.40 with displayed CE0.
claims.caveat: This is a specific input shift, not unseen factory/tool/material qualification.

claims.statement: Checklist3 says no major theoretical result, while TheoremA.1 is present; Checklist7 cites SMSE and sample residual variability for significance.
claims.caveat: The checklist is reporting evidence, not proof of theorem validity or a repeated-run statistical significance test.

claims.statement: The paper focuses on equality constraints and identifies inequality extension and Jacobian structure as future directions.
claims.caveat: No arbitrary industrial inequality/tolerance certificate is asserted.

claims.statement: The official accepted PDF directly identifies Python and experimental Julia repositories.
claims.caveat: Publication-time code promises and current pinned asset availability are separate observations.

records.title: Physics vs Distributions: Pareto Optimal Flow Matching with Physics Constraints
records.review_scope: Targeted methods/benchmark/execution source review;complete extracted text of pages6,7,16-19,21and selected earlier method passages. Remainder not claimed as reviewed.

claims.statement: Darcy data contain pressure and permeability on64x64 grids,10k training/1k validation samples, and no conditioning inputs; authors identify limited real-world representativeness.

Permeability reference is exp(G(x)), with zero-flux boundaries and a pressure integral condition. The paper uses matched numerical stencils for training/data generation rather than an external manufacturing measurement.
Table2 calls RE residual MSE while Fig3-4/prose refer to MAE; current public sampling code computes residual.abs().mean(). Metric identity must be reconciled before numeric reproduction claims.

Darcy comparison uses1024samples; D-Flow keeps888 under an RE<5 filter, and ECI enforces boundary conditions but not the nonlinear PDE residual. Methods do not have identical retained-case or constraint scopes.
The scale-normalization ablation has different reported RE/WD values than the main table. Source scaling and sampling variants must be bound to any comparison.
Dynamic stall uses simulated NACA0012 airfoil conditions and algebraic ideal-gas/skin-friction relations, not the Darcy trial conducted here; acquired dynamic-stall weights were not executed.
PBFM couples flow matching and physical residual objectives at training via conflict-free updates; inference-time constraint projection is not the mechanism of this audited sampler.
